stem: A fruit seller in Hyderabad buys \(n\) kilograms of mangoes for a total of \(C\) rupees. He sells all of the mangoes at a price per kilogram that is 20 rupees more than the price per kilogram he paid. Which expression represents his profit, in rupees, on the mangoes?
solution: He paid \(\frac{C}{n}\) rupees per kilogram, so he sells at \(\frac{C}{n} + 20\) rupees per kilogram.
Profit is revenue minus cost: \(C + 20n - C = 20n\).

explanation.A: Correct. Each of the \(n\) kilograms earns 20 rupees more than it cost, so the profit is \(20n\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the total revenue, not the profit; the cost \(C\) still has to be subtracted.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the cost from \(20n\) instead of from the revenue \(C + 20n\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the profit on a single kilogram, not on all \(n\) kilograms.

verify:
n, C = symbols('n C')
t = n*(C/n + 20) - C
assert simplify(value(choices[answer]) - t) == 0
assert all(simplify(value(choices[k]) - t) != 0 for k in choices if k != answer)
